source: The factor weights FICO publishes for its general-purpose scores, and the reporting periods set by the Fair Credit Reporting Act. Weights are FICO's own published shares; the VantageScore models weigh the same material differently.
confidenceNote: A score is computed by a bureau from a file this app cannot see. Nothing here produces a number. These are the factors, their published weights, and how long things stay — enough to know what moves a score and roughly how much, and not enough to pretend to one.
note: Ordered by weight. `youCanSee` says whether this app holds anything bearing on the factor; where it is false the room says so rather than guessing.

factors.label: Paying on time
factors.what: Whether you have paid at least the minimum, by the due date, on every account.
factors.moves: One payment 30 days late is the single most damaging ordinary event. Under 30 days late is usually a fee, not a report — lenders generally do not report until 30 days.
factors.lever: Autopay the minimum on everything, then pay more by hand. The minimum is what protects the file; the extra is what clears the debt.

factors.label: How much of your limit you are using
factors.what: Revolving balances against revolving limits — your cards, not your loans.
factors.moves: It is measured on the day the issuer reports, usually the statement date, not the due date. A card paid in full every month can still report high if you spend most of the limit before the statement closes.
factors.lever: Pay part of the balance BEFORE the statement date, not just before the due date. It is the fastest thing on this list to change: it re-reports monthly and carries no memory.

factors.label: How long you have had credit
factors.what: The age of your oldest account and the average age of all of them.
factors.moves: Closing an old card you no longer use shortens the average and removes its limit, which pushes utilisation up at the same time. Two harms from one tidy-up.
factors.lever: Keep the oldest no-fee card open and put one small recurring charge on it.

factors.label: The kinds of credit you hold
factors.what: Whether you have both revolving accounts (cards) and instalment accounts (loans).
factors.moves: The smallest ordinary factor. It is not worth taking on a loan you do not need.
factors.lever: Nothing to do. It fills in on its own as life happens.

factors.label: Recent applications
factors.what: Hard enquiries from applying, and how many accounts you have opened lately.
factors.moves: Rate-shopping for one mortgage, car or student loan counts once if the enquiries fall inside the same short window — the models are built for it. Applying for four cards in a month does not.
factors.lever: Do your rate shopping in one fortnight, not spread over a season.

howLongThingsStay.label: A late payment or a collection
howLongThingsStay.note: From the date of the first missed payment that led to it — not from the date it was paid.

howLongThingsStay.label: A PAID medical collection
howLongThingsStay.note: Removed from consumer reports once paid. Unpaid medical collections under $500 are no longer reported at all.

howLongThingsStay.label: A hard enquiry
howLongThingsStay.note: Stops affecting most scores after about one.

yourRights.what: Your report from each of the three bureaus, free, weekly
yourRights.where: annualcreditreport.com — the only site the law names. It is a report, not a score.

yourRights.what: A dispute the bureau must investigate, usually within 30 days
yourRights.where: Free, directly with the bureau. Nothing a repair firm can do for a fee is unavailable to you at no cost.

yourRights.what: A freeze and an unfreeze, free, at any time
yourRights.where: Each bureau separately. It stops new credit being opened in your name and does not affect your score.
